english.title: Unlawful disclosure of information for enforcing warrants
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally or recklessly

(A)_[disclosed information supplied under section 125C of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980 otherwise than as permitted by that section]_
(B)_[used information supplied under section 125C of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980 otherwise than for the purpose of facilitating the enforcement of a warrant under section 125A of that Act]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 125C of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980.

english.notes:
(i) Section 125A of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980 enables civilian enforcement officers to execute warrants of arrest, commitment, detention or distress warrants issued by a justice of the peace
(ii) Section 125C(3) provides that information for the purpose of executing a section 125A warrant may be supplied to
(a) any person entitled to execute the warrant
(b) any employee of a body or person who, for the purposes of section 125B, is an approved enforcement agency in relation to the warrant
(c) any justices' clerk or other person appointed under section 2(1) of the Courts Act 2003
(iii) Section 125C(5) provides that it is not an offence (a) to disclose any information in accordance with any enactment or order of a court or for the purposes of any proceedings before a court; or (b) to disclose any information which has previously been disclosed to the public.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: A fine.

Time Limit on Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
